name: Israel in the days of the Judges
charge: Making leagues with the inhabitants of the land; marrying their daughters and serving their gods; every man doing that which was right in his own eyes
summary: An angel came up from Gilgal to Bochim and rehearsed the covenant: the Lord had said He would never break it, and Israel was to make no league with the inhabitants of the land and to tear down their altars, and they had not listened. The sentence was that He would not drive those nations out, but leave them as thorns in Israel’s sides and their gods as a snare. A generation arose that did not know the Lord, lived among the very nations it had been commanded to destroy, married their daughters and served their gods, and was sold into the hands of one oppressor after another. The key to the whole book is one verse: there was no king in Israel, and every man did what was right in his own eyes.
offenseFull: An angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim and reminded Israel of the covenant: the Lord had brought them out of Egypt into the land promised to their fathers, with a plain command to make no league with the people of the land and to tear down their altars, and they had not listened (Judges 2:1-5). The law had said it before they crossed over: no covenant with those nations or their gods, and no room for them in the land, or they would lead Israel into sin (Exodus 23:32-33). Living among them breeds curiosity about their gods, and that curiosity is the snare: how did these nations serve their gods, what is that thing they are doing with that tree, what are they hanging on it (Deuteronomy 12:30). Tearing down their altars meant burning the carved images and not even wanting the silver or gold on them (Deuteronomy 7:25). The same is true where we are scattered. We have made leagues with the inhabitants of the land, in their sports leagues and bowling leagues and at their dinner parties, when the scripture warns against envying the violent man or copying any of his ways (Proverbs 3:31).

When Joshua and his generation died, another generation grew up that did not know the Lord or what He had done for Israel, and they served the Baals and Ashtaroth, the gods of the nations around them (Judges 2:10-13). A pattern starts there: when a judge in Israel dies, the people just go off. It shows we are a people that need leadership, which is why we are told to trust the Lord and not rely on our own understanding (Proverbs 3:5-6). Brothers and sisters today come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television. Israel lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, the very nations they were told to utterly destroy, married their daughters and served their gods (Judges 3:5-6; Deuteronomy 7:1-4; Deuteronomy 20:16-18). Joshua had warned that if they intermarried with what was left of these nations, the Lord would stop driving them out and they would become snares and traps (Joshua 23:12-13). The key to the whole book is one verse: there was no king in Israel, and every man did what was right in his own eyes (Judges 17:6). With no king and no government Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and the same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you.
judgmentFull: The sentence at Bochim was that the Lord would not drive those nations out; they would be thorns in Israel’s sides and their gods a snare, and the people wept aloud. In His anger He handed Israel over to raiders and to their enemies, until they could no longer stand against them (Judges 2:14-15). Look at us today, hands up and do not shoot, begging our enemies to see us as people. That is the curse written for disobedience, a curse that follows a man out of his house and back into it (Deuteronomy 28:19). We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people, with individual millionaires and no farms, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain itself. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy hands you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums to live in and bad food to eat, he is at war with you. The Lord has withdrawn to His place until we acknowledge our offence (Hosea 5:15).

Still He raised up judges who rescued them from the raiders, because He was moved by their groaning under those who oppressed them (Judges 2:16-19), as in Egypt, where He said He had seen the affliction of His people (Exodus 3:7). Israel is the apple of His eye, and to touch them is to touch Him (Zechariah 2:8). The Most High does not want to see us on the bottom, but we broke His commandments and had to be punished for it. Yet they would not listen to their judges, and when a judge died they became more corrupt than their fathers. As soon as we came out of the condition we were in, we went right back to it. So He left the nations Joshua had not driven out, to test whether Israel would keep His way as their fathers had, and to teach the younger generations war (Judges 2:20-23; Judges 3:1-4). Judges is the record of that affliction beginning to come upon our people for turning their backs on the one true living God.

lawsResolved.text: National punishment, captivity, curses and destruction for idolatry or worshiping false gods in the land.
Disobedience to God causes national captivity by heathen or enemy nations.
Backsliding from God's ways causes punishment and the loss of His protection.
We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.

text.text: And an angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim, and said, I made you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you unto the land which I sware unto your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you.
And ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice: why have ye done this?
Wherefore I also said, I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you.
And it came to pass, when the angel of the Lord spake these words unto all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept.
And they called the name of that place Bochim: and they sacrificed there unto the Lord.
Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.

Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.
Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim:

And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the people that were round about them, and bowed themselves unto them, and provoked the Lord to anger.
And they forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites:
And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

When the Lord thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, and hath cast out many nations before thee, the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou;
And when the Lord thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them:
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.
But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth:
But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee:
That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the Lord your God.
Else if ye do in any wise go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and shall make marriages with them, and go in unto them, and they to you:

Know for a certainty that the Lord your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which the Lord your God hath given you.
In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed.
Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.
I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.

And yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but they went a whoring after other gods, and bowed themselves unto them: they turned quickly out of the way which their fathers walked in, obeying the commandments of the Lord; but they did not so.

And when the Lord raised them up judges, then the Lord was with the judge, and delivered them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.

And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.
And the Lord said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel; and he said, Because that this people hath transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened unto my voice;
I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations which Joshua left when he died:
That through them I may prove Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not.
Therefore the Lord left those nations, without driving them out hastily; neither delivered he them into the hand of Joshua.
Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof;
Namely, five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal–hermon unto the entering in of Hamath.
And they were to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
